items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: I remember one night at the Apex Club... Les Hylte brought his band in from Culver City... Les Hylte was pretty well established

ctx.x: Now, after that experience with them, I'm gonna try and be specific about the years which is always, as I told you, it's hard for me to do.

Okay. It seems to me right about this time was when Buck Clayton had formed a band called The Fourteen Gentlemen of Harlem, and Les Hylte was at the Cotton Club, and he had a drummer which was Lionel Hampton, which was with Les Hylte. But Buck Clayton had a drummer -- I got it -- his name was Baby Lewis; he was a left handed drummer, and he was a very, very smooth drummer, and I remember one night at the Apex Club, you know, after I had started playing music, they had a Battle of the Bands at the Apex Club, and…

And Buck Clayton was the younger new band coming up, and Les Hylte was pretty well established because he broadcasted every night on KHEJ, too, incidentally, twice a night, as a matter of fact -- used to listen to both broadcasts, and he had Lionel Hampton with him, and had a great trumpet player with him named Lloyd Reese -- I'm surayou must have heard of Lloyd Reese.
